## Chapter Eight

Recovery



Lucas awoke three days later to the steady beeping of medical equipment. Looking around the large room, he could see beds lined along both walls and he realized he was in some sort of medical unit. He could see a doctor speaking into a terminal, arguing with someone but he could only hear half of the conversation, he chose instead to focus his eyes on his surroundings and his ears on the doctor. “You kept him in there too long, any longer and he would have died, I am not even sure he is sane. We have his muscles attached to electrical TEMS units to try and rebuild them. He is on constant Intravenous nutrition, but I don’t know if he will ever fully recover” the doctor said sternly to whoever was on the other end.



Lucas didn’t care, he was just happy to be able to see and to have the constant visits from his family and friends over. Did they actually visit him? He wondered still assessing the room, twenty four beds, two cameras per bed, one guard at each end he thought and tried to move his arms and legs, they was a little play but they had tied him down, wires coming out from under the covers and an odd tingling from all over both arms and legs told him that he had all his limbs, but he was restrained in the bed. Even the slight movement exhausted him and he put his head on the pillow to rest, he needed rest his body felt worn. He concentrated on the doctor as he rested his eyes. “It will be months until he will be ready for general population again, I don’t even know if he will ever walk again sir” the doctor continued, was he talking about me? Lucas wondered again flexing his legs and decided it couldn’t be, he could feel his legs and he knew how to walk right, he walked… before right. He tried to remember before the void and it was fuzzy, he remembered people, remembered books but it wasn’t clear, this should have bothered him, but he was too tired and slowly his mind fell to unconsciousness sinking deep into a healing sleep.



He woke again two days later, he felt better, more himself he thought as he looked around at the large room and watched as one of the silver saucer drones patrolled the path between the rows of beds. Six beds down a doctor and a nurse were consulting the hologram of a patience body as it floated four feet above him. The doctor pointed at various points along the leg of the hologram allowing him to zoom in and take notes in the air next to the limb. The nurse paid astute attention, leaning over the small console attached to the top of the bed and hitting buttons that changed the color of the patient’s IV bag. Lucas laid there watching, transfixed over the entire event, looking at his own IV bag he noticed it was a deep green and somewhere in the back of his mind he remembered a doctor talking about feeding through an IV, was that him he thought or another patient.



Lucas could still feel the constant tingling of whatever they had attached to his limbs as the electric shock stiffened and then let loose various muscles, he thought he felt a little stronger today. Closing his eyes, he thanked whomever that he had not had visits from his father or mother since getting out of the dark place, and he vowed never to go back there, it had almost broken him and he thought another trip would truly send him over the edge. Randomly he wondered if Dyson missed him, as odd as it was, he missed the salty old man and also Lopez his hard-hitting weight trainer and looked forward to getting back to his cell, and back to training.



The doctor finished up and with a wave of his arm the holo of the patient disappeared. He looked around and noticed Lucas awake and staring at him. He turned and whispered to the nurse and then the older grey-haired physician slowly made his way over to Lucas. He tried to sit up in bed but was still held down by restraints, he opted for scooting his pillow up using his shoulders so his head would be propped.



The doctor arrived pinning his shirt in back of his pants stretching the material over the modest gut he sported and examined a small tablet that he produced from within the pocket of the lab coat. “Mister Christian, its good to see you awake, you had us worried for a bit” he began pleasantly enough, Lucas could almost imagine he wasn’t in prison but at a real doctor’s office, almost he thought with a smile. “Thank you doctor, I am feeling much better, when can I get out of here?” Lucas asked cautiously causing the doctor to tsk and shake his head. “You still have a lot of recovery to do , I’m sorry to say you will be here for another two weeks and then another thirty days in the recovery wing for physical therapy before we can release you back to your cell” he answered his eyes never leaving the little tablet. Lucas cocked his head and eyed the older man “What is wrong with me doc?” he asked not sure he wanted to know, but needed to. The doctor blew out a breath and then touched the tablet probably going to a different screen or tab thought Lucas. After a moment he finally looked up at him. Lucas could see the empathy in the doctor’s eyes and appreciated it, that was something he had not seen in anyone In years. “You muscles need to be rebuilt, they suffered severe atrophy, you were mal nourished and your retinas had to have a small laser alteration after the damage of so long prolonged to the absolute darkness caused.” He said “but over all you will recover, we were worried about your legs for a while, and it required minor corrective surgery, I don’t know if you know this but you had a hairline fracture that wasn’t fixed and was causing some problems. But we were able to repair it and your going to be fine” he said again smiling. Lucas couldn’t remember breaking his leg, or fracturing it , he tried to remember his time in the void and couldn’t recall the type of pain that would have accompanied an injury like that, but he was pretty much out of it he thought. “How long was I in there doc?” Lucas asked causing the doctor to shoot him a worried stare before he peered around the room to see where the nurse was. “I am not supposed to tell you because you were in there a lot longer than anyone is authorized to be in solitary, but you should know that the warden had you secured in that room for one year and six months, that is the reason your injuries were so extensive. And the only reason you are here and not back in general population is I threatened to turn him in to the prison board should he go against my recommendations” the doctor said triumphantly. Then he leaned in almost conspiratorially “Apparently you seemed to have made the man angry and he is still trying to punish you for it, what did you do to him young man?” the doctor asked the curiosity was killing him, it didn’t take a detective to see that. He thought about it for a moment and then shot a gently smile to the old quack “I defended myself sir, I merely defended myself” and then he shut his eyes on the confused doctor and tried to relax.



The nurse shook Lucas awake sometime later and proceeded to give him a sponge bath, though with the restraints and electric wires sticking out all around it was not very thorough. She changed his bandages and adjusted his IV, nodding to him, she proceeded down the line to the next patient on her rounds.



Lucas closed his eyes but was started awake by someone lightly whistling in his direction, he looked over to the bed next to him to find a bespectacled bald little fat man grinning with a full set of half eroded and yellowing teeth in his mouth. Lucas eyed him , trying to figure out if this guy was even sane as he just lay there smiling like a fool at him. “What you in fer” said the main with an odd southern draw that Lucas had never heard before. First he thought about ignoring him, but then realized, he wasn’t that tired and really had nothing much else to do, in the end he figured at the very least it would be entertaining. Lucas leaned over a little and whispered “Treason, you?” he said, causing the guys smile to falter a little, and then it returned with the wattage turned up “Murder” he said pleasantly.



Lucas wasn’t sure where to go with that, and now he wasn’t so sure he should have ignored the guy. “did you do it?” he asked him, and the pudgy cheeks vibrated a little as he enthusiastically shook his head “Oh yeah, definitely, and you?” he shot back. Lucas shook his head “nope”. He simply said. The guy seemed to expect the answer, as pretty much every convict will tell you he is innocent of anything that got him sent to prison, well except for this guy apparently Lucas thought. But he seemed pleasant enough aside from the desperate need for a dentist. “You need to get to psychiatric, you need to be crazy” the man said, rocking now in his bed. Lucas looked him over, yup shitbag crazy he thought but he had nothing better to do , might as well eat up some time. “Okay, why is that old man” he said , taking a scan around the room, the action ingrained into him from years of training with Dyson. The man sat there smiling at him and for a long time he didn’t speak, almost to the point Lucad thought he had lost him and then suddenly his face was serious, sane , the old man’s eyes burning with intelligence and drive as he leaned forward ensuring Lucas could see them “Becausde you have made an enemy of the Warden, he is going to chew you up and spit you out, using the inmates and the prison to do it. I don’t know exactly what you did, but I heard the guards talking, you are going downtown when they let you out of here” he said, his eyes loosing focus and laying back he began to hum a tune, he was no longer there, no longer paying attention. Lucas tried a few times to get the man’s attention, but he had checked out. “Dammit” Lucas whispered. This wasn’t good, if the Warden truly was pissed putting him downtown would be a death sentence, especially in his present state, he was in no shape to defend himself right now.



When he had been here a year, Lucas had caught a few conversations about downtown, which was what the inmates called maximum security , tier four inmates, these were lifers, guys with nothing to lose and they were next to impossible to control, according to rumor the drones would stun once and then instantly kill inmates if they continued to disobey. Going downtown was absolutely a death sentence.



The only thing he could think of was that Grigor and Anton were his somehow, that the Warden owned them and by killing them he had gotten on the sadistic prick’s radar. He had never had direct dealings with Warden Parsons, which from what he had heard, was a good thing. Brian Parsons had been Warden of this prison going on forty years and was now only a few years from retirement, to look at him you would see a kindly old grandfather, but if even half the stories he had overheard were true, the man was in control of most of the smuggling of drugs, weapons and more into the prison, there was a story of a convict who had tried to turn him in to the prison board because the Warden had screwed him on a shipment, they found him in the exercise yard cut into eight pieces and to add insult to injury, his cell mate and business partner was framed for it, so Parson’s had gotten rid of them both in one fell swoop.



He needed a way to stall for time, he needed to get back into shape if the Warden was going to put him downtown after this. For a moment he thought about Psychiatric, but then Lucas remembered the empathetic look the doctor had given him, and the guy had stood up to the warden, so maybe he could get dear old doc to put him in physical therapy for a bit. He thought smiling now, He would have a talk with the doctor in the morning he finished as his head hit the pillow and his eyes got heavy, as bed time came around at the prison, sedatives were released into the all the patients IV bags like clockwork, only a mild dose ,but enough to knock them out for the night and give the nurse some peace.



The next morning Lucas awoke and looked around the room already finding the doctor doing his rounds, he would have to wait until he got closer. Another hour and Lucas flagged him over. “Doc, I need your help” he started , getting a surprised look at the doctor. “I don’t usually take requests young man” he said his face spreading into a disapproving frown.



Lucas took a breath and leveled an earnest gaze at the old man. “Doc, I know you care about your patients, I am not asking for anything illegal, I just need your recommendation to be transferred to Physical therapy after this, they are going to move me to the lifers wing and I am in no shape to defend myself, please doctor, you would be saving my life” Lucas finished certain he wasn’t exaggerating that last part.



The doctor paused, looking at Lucas and he could see the wheels turning in his brain. After a moment he nodded “I was going to anyway, the Warden did try to insist that you be transferred immediately, but I overruled him, its my prerogative on how my patients are treated, I do believe you would benefit from recovery and exercise before returning to general population” the Doctor agreed Lucas was surprised at the ease of the doctor to agree, but he wouldn’t look a gift horse in the mouth “Thank you Doctor” Lucas breathed, settling back in the bed.



It was just under a week when the orderlies wheeled Lucas out and down the short hall to the Rehab unit. He found himself in a private cell with a screen next to the door that held an itinerary for him. Smiling he read through the exercise routines and the private yard time that rehab got, that would allow him some time with the weights too, he didn’t know how much time he had, but he would take advantage of every second.



The first day they left him in the room to get acclimated, but instead of lying in bed, he began a regiment of push-ups and sit-up’s, struggling through the first set, his body felt like it was on fire as he willed his muscles to lift his body weight.



He collapsed after a set of twenty and curled into s ball a string of muffled curses thrown out at the room. This was not going to be easy he thought. And for the first time in since seeing Grigor and Anton again, he felt afraid, if he was put downtown now, he would be dead in a day.



The second day, they took a small group to water therapy, Lucas didn’t even know there was a pool in the prison, it wasn’t grand or large, more like a five-foot-deep round wading pool, but it did allow four of his fellow inmates to perform basic exercises using the water resistance to help build there muscles. Lucas pushed himself, every thought turning towards his current physical state and the ticking clock until the Warden got what he wanted and Lucas was transferred downtown.



He felt the muscles burning and shooting pains as if the muscle was tearing like paper ran up his legs, but he pushed harder, he didn’t have the luxury of taking it slow. He felt a hand on his shoulder and looked up to see a middle age man with kind features leaning over the edge of the pool and looking at him “Son, don’t push that hard, you are going to hurt yourself, do the exercise set only” he said gently. Lucas smiled and nodded at the man, he would have to be careful, if they disqualified him because he wasn’t following instructions, that could be grounds enough to transfer him.



So he set his face into a neutral grimace, not allowing the pain to show on his face as he continued to push. By the time the session was over, and the guards had begun herding the inmates to bring them back to there assigned cells, Lucas could barely move, every motion sent pain running up his legs, arms and back. He was in worse shape then he thought. Concentrating he did his best to not allow the pain to show in his face, he wanted the trainer to think all was well, and he managed to do that all the way back to the cell. Once there, he walked over to the far corner directly under the camera and curled himself into a ball, finally allowing the grimace and a hiss trying to vent the pain out of his body. He spent the first week repeating the same thing, pushing his body, hiding the pain until he could get back to that same corner in the cell, ensuring the staff were none the wiser.



At the end of the week, the pain was still there, but with the pain came recognition that he could move faster, that slowly, ever so slowly his muscles were regaining the ability to move normally again. He knew it would be a long time until he was back to where he had been, but this was progress, and progress could save his life.



At the end of week two, the pain had subsided, it became much easier to hide his discomfort and he was able to push himself further. Though he kept watch on the trainer who had more than once gotten suspicious that Lucas was doing more than he was assigned, but he never said anything, opting instead to shoot him mildly disapproving looks from time to time.



Lucas would go from session to session, between the pool and the light aerobics to working out in the yard, when he got back to his room, it was push-ups and sit ups as well as reviewing his martial training to ensure he didn’t lose his edge. If that crazy fucker was to be believed, Lucas would need it.



He wanted to get a message to Dyson, he didn’t know how he could so he put it out of his mind, if Dyson wanted to know, he had the resources to find out what had happened to Lucas, but he didn’t know if the old man would or did, or even if he had the power to change his oncoming fate would he. None of this is helping thought Lucas and put it out of his mind. During his time I the rehab unit, Lucas was unaware he had turned twenty four and spent his birthday pushing himself against the impending clock.
